actions.text: My notes say that trimming per-call setup and inlining wrappers did not reach the 1% bar, and inlining actually made things worse. So this time I'll work on the encode digit loop itself, building on the accepted base**4 grouping rather than redoing it.

actions.diff:
--- a/base58/__init__.py
+++ b/base58/__init__.py
@@ -141,5 +141,24 @@
-    pairs, sq, big, big3, zero = tables
-    parts = []
-    while i >= big3:
-        # Four groups of four digits per pass while at least four remain
-        i, rem = divmod(i, big)
+    pairs, sq, big, big3, zero = tables
+    parts = []
+    big7 = big3 * big3 * big
+    while i >= big7:
+        # Eight groups of four digits per pass while at least eight remain
+        i, rem = divmod(i, big)
+        i, rem2 = divmod(i, big)
+        i, rem3 = divmod(i, big)
+        i, rem4 = divmod(i, big)
+        i, rem5 = divmod(i, big)
+        i, rem6 = divmod(i, big)
+        i, rem7 = divmod(i, big)
+        i, rem8 = divmod(i, big)
+        parts += (pairs[rem % sq], pairs[rem // sq],
+                  pairs[rem2 % sq], pairs[rem2 // sq],
+                  pairs[rem3 % sq], pairs[rem3 // sq],
+                  pairs[rem4 % sq], pairs[rem4 // sq],
+                  pairs[rem5 % sq], pairs[rem5 // sq],
+                  pairs[rem6 % sq], pairs[rem6 // sq],
+                  pairs[rem7 % sq], pairs[rem7 // sq],
+                  pairs[rem8 % sq], pairs[rem8 // sq])
+    if i >= big3:
+        # Four to seven groups remain: take four of them
+        i, rem = divmod(i, big)

actions.reason: Tried taking eight base**4 groups per pass in b58encode (with a single four-group block before the existing tail, and base**28 kept in the cached tables). Outputs were identical and the guards passed, but encode_ir only reached a ratio of 0.9956 against the required 0.9900. Meanwhile decode_ir rose to 1.0008 and check_ir to 1.0038. By my rough count, the remaining encode cost per call is one divmod and two small-int operations per four digits, plus a fixed setup cost. All of that is close to the floor for this approach in CPython. Most of the measured total is interpreter startup and the harness itself. Splitting large inputs in half by base**(4k) saves only about 10% of the limb work on the long blobs, because CPython's division is schoolbook. That is too little to reach 1%. I see no honest change to this design that clears the bar, so I am submitting nothing.

journal.text:
Test agent here. I worked on b58encode in base58/__init__.py. I tried taking eight base**4 groups per pass instead of fewer. I added a single four-group block before the existing tail. I kept base**28 in the cached tables. Same bytes out was the bar.

Outputs were identical. Guards passed, one file, 32 lines. encode_ir went from 212887338 to 211947104, a ratio of 0.9956. The required ratio was 0.9900, so it was rejected. decode_ir rose to 1.0008. check_ir rose to 1.0038. Small drift, but the wrong way. Choppy water, and not much tide under it.

I now believe bigger groups alone do not move encode enough. The inner divmod loop is not where most of the cost sits for these inputs. That is a belief. Not measured yet.

I did not submit a candidate. Next I will profile one encode call and count big-int operations per output char. Then I pick the step that dominates.
